questions.q: How does a supporting reference differ from an account segment?
options: They are the same thing with two different names
An account segment applies to every transaction across the whole ledger; a supporting reference attaches extra detail to one specific journal line without becoming a permanent segment
Supporting references can only be used in Receivables
Supporting references replace the need for account rules
questions.explain: Account segments are a fixed part of the Chart of Accounts used everywhere; supporting references carry transaction-specific detail at the subledger journal line level.

questions.q: Why might adding a new Chart of Accounts segment just to track supplier number be a bad idea?
options: It would be impossible; Oracle does not allow new segments
Because that segment would apply to every account combination in the ledger and would grow as the supplier list grows, even on lines unrelated to a supplier
Supplier number can never be tracked anywhere in Oracle Fusion
It would make the ledger run out of currencies
questions.explain: A full segment change is permanent and ledger-wide; a supporting reference avoids bloating the Chart of Accounts for detail that only matters on certain lines.

questions.q: What is a third-party control account?
options: A bank account owned by a third-party vendor
A single GL account, like Accounts Payable Trade, that represents a combined balance owed to or from many individual parties at once
An account that can only be viewed by external auditors
A segment value reserved for tax authorities
questions.explain: A third-party control account, like AP Trade, holds the combined balance for many suppliers (or customers) in one GL account.

questions.q: In the worked example, what did the supporting reference on the AP accrual line carry?
options: The invoice due date only
A GL account segment value
The supplier number (10452, for Meridian Supply Co.)
Nothing; the line had no supporting reference
questions.explain: The example attached a Supplier Number supporting reference identifying Meridian Supply Co. on the accrual line.

questions.q: What does attaching a supplier-number supporting reference to AP Trade lines ultimately make possible?
options: Automatically paying suppliers without approval
Breaking the combined AP Trade balance down by individual supplier for reconciliation, something the account segment alone cannot provide
Eliminating the need for the Accounts Payable Trade account entirely
Changing the ledger's functional currency
questions.explain: Supporting references enable reconciliation reports that group a shared control account's balance by individual third party, such as supplier or customer.
